verses.1: On taking up a bow Rama saw Kumbhakarna of extraordinary energy, prodigious, and of large body, adorned with a crown.
verses.2: That foremost of Rakshasas was like a mountain in appearance, it was like Lord Narayana taking steps to the sky earlier.
verses.3: Seeing the Rakshasa who was like a rainy cloud with water, decked with gold ornaments, the commander in chief of Vanaras ran.
verses.4: Seeing the army scared away and the army of Rakshasas growing in size, Rama was astonished and thus spoke to Vibheeshana.
verses.5: "Who is that hero resembling a mountain, a crowned one with tawny eyes, looking like a rainy cloud driven by lightning? He is seen in Lanka."
verses.6: "He is seen here like a lone comet on earth. Seeing him the Vanaras are fleeing hither and thither."
verses.7: "Who is he, that gigantic Rakshasa? Is he a demon or perhaps a colossus? No such being was seen by me earlier."
verses.8: Asked by the prince Rama, of unwearied action, highly intelligent Vibheeshana spoke.
verses.9: "Vyvasvatha (Lord of death) as well as Vasava (Indra) were defeated by him in war. He is Kumbhakarna, the son of sage Visrava, a stupendous one and there is no other Rakshasa who equals him in size."
verses.10: "O Raghava! In war Devas, Danavas, Yakshas, Nagas, ogres, Gandharvas, Vidydharas, Kinneras in thousands were defeated by him."
verses.11: "This Kumbhakarna with pike in hand and fierce eyes, is mighty strong. All the Devatas could not kill him, deluded that he is death personified."
verses.12: "Kumbhakarna is by nature (by birth) energetic and mighty. The strength of other Rakshasas is on account of their boons received by them."
verses.13: " As soon as he was born, he was hungry and this great soul being strong consumed thousands of created beings."
verses.14: "In that way when Kumbhakarna was devouring, out of fear all people sought the refuge of Indra and represented."
verses.15: "Mahendra who was armed with thunderbolt got enraged and hurt Kumbhakarna with thunderbolt. He reeled and roared with the strike."
verses.16: "People were already afraid of Kumbhakarna, and after hearing the lion roar of this Rakshasa they were even more scared."
verses.17: "Then mighty Kumbhakarna, who was enraged, pulled out the tusk of Airavatham and struck at the chest of Indra."
verses.18: "Hit by Kumbhakarna Indra felt tormented. The Devatas, Brahmarshis and Danavas became despondent. Accompanied by created beings they complained to Brahma."
verses.19: "They reported to Brahma about Kumbhakarna's ruthless deeds, devouring created beings, insulting, harsh and also destroying the abodes of sages violently and abducting others' wives."
verses.20: "They reported to Brahma about Kumbhakarna's ruthless deeds, devouring created beings, insulting, harsh and also destroying the abodes of sages violently and abducting others' wives."
verses.21: "If he consumes created beings every day like that, in the course of time the world will be devoid of beings."
verses.22: Hearing the words of Indra, Brahma conjured the Rakshasas and saw Kumbhakarna with them.
verses.23: "Beholding Kumbhakarna, Brahma was alarmed and spoke to him to restore the confidence of Kumbhakarna."
verses.24: "Surely you are begotten by Paulastya for the destruction of the universe. Therefore, remain sleeping like a dead one from today, ' said Brahma and cursed him."
verses.25: "Thereafter, by the curse of Lord Brahma, Kumbhakarna fell in front. Highly agitated at this Ravana spoke these words to Brahma."
verses.26: "Oh Brahma! Cutting a golden tree at the stage of fruiting is not fair. It is not proper for you to curse your great grandson in that way."
verses.27: "Your words will not become untrue, no doubt. Sleep, he must but waking time may be fixed."
verses.28: On hearing Ravana's words, Brahma said" He will sleep for six months and stay awake for a day."
verses.29: "This hero will open his mouth wide and move about and alone he will consume the world like the swollen fire."
verses.30: "Overtaken by worry, the king out of fear of your prowess just awakened sleeping Kumbhakarna."
verses.31: "This heroic Kumbhakarna has come out of his residence extremely angry and going to and from to consume all Vanaras."
verses.32: "On merely seeing Kumbhakarna, the monkeys are running away. How will they check him who is enraged in war?"
verses.33: "Let all the Vanaras be told, that this one standing high is a machine then the Vanaras will not be scared of victory."
verses.34: Hearing the words of Vibheeshana, which was reasonable and, in their favour, Raghava said this to Nila, the commander in chief of the army.
verses.35: "Pavaka, go and organize all the army and get together to occupy all the gates, highways, bridges in Lanka."
verses.36: "Be ready staying on mountain tops, trees, rocks armed with weapons and rocks in hand."
verses.37: As instructed by Raghava, the monkey leader Nila, elephant among the monkeys, ordered the monkey troops as instructed.
verses.38: Then taking mountains, Gavaksha, Sarabha, Hanuman, Angada who looked like mountains themselves marched to the gate.
verses.39: The monkeys desiring to be triumphant, took trees and began to strike at the enemies on hearing Rama's control.
verses.40: Then Vanaras taking trees and mountains in their shining hand s marching close to each other seemed like a huge mass of terrible clouds hanging close to a mountain. ।।इत्यार्षेवाल्मीकीयेश्रीमद्रामायणेआदिकाव्येयुद्धकाण्डेषष्टितमस्सर्गः ।। This is the end of the sixty first sarga of Yuddha Kanda of the first epic the holy Ramayana composed by sage Valmiki.
